newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says reviewing truck venture in India.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says reviewing truck venture in India.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Friday that it is reviewing its truck venture with Daewoo Corp in India.
An industrial newspaper reported that Toyota would pull out of its Indian truck venture with South Korea's Daewoo to focus on making passenger cars in the country.

When asked about that report, a Toyota spokeswoman said: "We are conducting a feasibility study on production of passenger cars in India and in relation to that, we are considering our relations with DCM Daewoo in the future."

Toyota currently has a 2.5 percent stake in DCM Daewoo Ltd and if it sells its stake in the venture, that means that the Japanese car maker would no longer assemble trucks in India, another company spokeswoman said.
Toyota and Daewoo have been jointly assembling Toyota trucks since 1984.
Daewoo has a 51 percent stake in DCM Daewoo, a Toyota spokesman said.
Toyota Motor said in August that it hoped to launch a joint venture to produce cars in cooperation with Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd, a Toyota Motor affiliate, and Indian financial group Kirloskar.
